title: Senior Armor SNCO (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC PP&O # #
raw_text:
7.     MOS 1869, Senior Armor SNCO (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC PP&O # #

    a. Summary. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF
ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL
BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY. The
Senior Armor SNCO serves as the senior enlisted technical and tactical
advisor to the commander on tank operations. Additionally, he advises the
commander on the condition, care and economical use of unit resources and
equipment. The Senior Armor SNCO coordinates and supervises all aspects of
the platoon, company or battalion operations, logistics and the
administrative requirements that affect unit readiness. He assists with the
development of the unit’s training plan and management of the unit readiness
program to ensure all task support the unit’s core and assigned mission
essential tasks. The Senior Armor SNCO serves as the principal mentor to all
marines in the armor community.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold PMOS 1812, Armor Marine.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (3) Marines seeking an MOS lateral move (LAT move) to MOS 1869 are
required to meet all prerequisites and requirements of PMOS 1812.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Gunnery Sergeants: successful completion of the Maneuver Senior
Leader’s Course (MSL-C) (A03KKX3) prior to being assigned the 1869 PMOS.

        (2) Master Sergeants: successful completion of the GCE Operations
Specialist Course (N30RCC1 or N30KBC1) or successful completion of the
Operations and Tactics Instructor Chief Course (M09HE35) prior to being
assigned the 1869 PMOS.

        (3) Master Gunnery Sergeants: successful completion of the
Operations and Tactics Instructor Course (M09HE35 or M09KYD5) prior to being
assigned the 1869 PMOS.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (m), Tank Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Armored Assault Vehicle Crew Members 55-3013.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Operations and Tactics Instructor, 0577.

            (2) Armor Marine, 1812.

            (3) GCE Operations Specialist, 8711.

# The 1869 PMOS will be awarded only after completing the MOS requirements.
To facilitate M&RA with assignments, Marines may be assigned using the



                                           3-137                        Enclosure (1)
 3119                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



intended MOS (IMOS) for which they were selected until they have met the
requirements.




                                    3-138                        Enclosure (1)
 3120                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: COMBAT VEHICLE 1. Introduction. The Tank, Assault Amphibious Vehicle and Amphibious Combat Vehicle OccFld includes operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance of tracked vehicles in the combined arms environment during both amphibious assaults and subsequent land operations ashore. Qualifications required include basic mechanical aptitude and the ability to perform harmoniously with others in the confined area inside combat vehicles. The duties involved are incident to the operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance of tanks and assault amphibious vehicles. Formal schooling is provided to Marines at both the entry level and at the appropriate time in career development. Marines entering this OccFld receive MOS 1800, Basic Tank and Assault Amphibious Marine. After entry into OccFld 18 and assignment of a basic 1800 MOS, personnel specialize in either the M1A1 Tank or the Assault Amphibious Vehicle are assigned MOS 1812, 1833, or 1834 respectively.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
